explanation: No single monarch makes the round trip. The return north takes several generations, yet each year a new generation finds its way to the same mountain forests.

claims.text: Monarch butterflies of eastern North America migrate to spend the winter in mountain forests of central Mexico.
Blue morphos, peacock butterflies and cabbage whites do not migrate from eastern North America to winter in Mexico.
No individual monarch completes the full round trip; the northward return takes several generations.
Each year a new generation of monarchs reaches the same wintering forests without ever having been there.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: four listed, all standard; 'several generations' carries no number word. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology, so none applies and every high-risk claim needs web evidence from checker A. rivalTest: the painted lady and the red admiral also migrate in North America, so neither is an option; the blue morpho lives in Central and South American forests, the peacock butterfly in Europe and Asia, and the cabbage white spends the winter as a pupa. The stem says eastern North America because western monarchs winter on the California coast. Argued against the key: the Mexican wintering forests are the textbook monarch story. An earlier draft asked for the country, but Mexico is a common answer across the bank, so dedupe kept pairing it with unrelated items. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: a North American migration, but the monarch is famous worldwide; I wrote 'each year' rather than a season name, so it reads the same in both hemispheres. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 26 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a multiple-choice item. doubts: none.

evidence.restatement: Eastern North American monarchs fly to oyamel fir forests in the mountains of central Mexico for the winter.
Blue morphos are tropical American, peacock butterflies Eurasian, and cabbage whites make no such migration.
The trip back north takes several generations; no single butterfly completes the round trip.
The generation that reaches the Mexican forests has never been there before.
Eastern North American monarchs overwinter in the mountain forests of central Mexico.
Blue morphos (tropical Americas), peacock butterflies (Eurasia) and cabbage whites do not make that migration.
No single monarch completes the whole round trip; the way back north takes several generations.
Each year's southbound generation reaches the same wintering forests although it has never been there.

issues.note: The explanation opens with "No butterfly makes the round trip", a universal statement. Claim c3 only supports "No individual monarch completes the full round trip". In context it reads fine, but "No monarch" would match the claim.
